coaching.headline: The middle game was a shitshow and the finish was a demolition: both Primal Fangtooths, the Orb Prime and nine structures to four.
coaching.team: The enemy led on kills early, then the team drew level at ten apiece before a 0-4 fight. That fight opened the only stretch where the enemy took structures: three allied outer towers and an inner tower, plus a Fangtooth and a Genesis Core. From the Primal Fangtooth fight on, the team won every fight but one, took both Primal Fangtooths, the Orb Prime and two Genesis Cores, then broke two inhibitors and the Core.

focus.title: One death, then everyone backs off
focus.action: When the first ally drops and the enemy still has more heroes standing in the fight, the rest call the retreat and fall back together. Feeding bodies in one at a time is a conga line, not a fight.

21.8.call: Terra killed Grux, Sparrow killed Murdock and Steel, and Lt. Belica killed Gadget. The fight went 0-4 while two allied outer towers fell in the same window, and the enemy added a Fangtooth soon after.

37.3.call: Gadget killed Lt. Belica and Sparrow, Grux killed Countess, Aurora killed Terra and Murdock killed Mourn. The fight went 5-0, the Primal Fangtooth fell to the team in the same window and an enemy inhibitor fell shortly after. That is the template: every enemy dead, then the base.

40.7.call: Grux killed Sparrow, Steel killed Mourn and Murdock killed Lt. Belica with no allied deaths, and the second enemy inhibitor fell in the same window. The enemy Core went down right after. With three enemies dead and an inhibitor open, the whole team commits to the Core.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks324 ran the support job properly: the most wards placed in the game, every enemy ward the team destroyed, the most assists in the game and the most damage mitigated on the team. Proper fucking work.

Steel died twice before the ten-minute mark, once to Sparrow outside any detected fight, and the enemy took the first Fangtooth shortly after. Before the next early Fangtooth, Steel waits for Murdock or Aurora before stepping toward the pit.
c2c329a0-75dc-41be-8894-cca296099061: Grux was the best player in this lobby: the most kills, most hero damage and most gold in the game, with hero damage per minute more than double the recorded Grux norm. An absolute fucking menace.
Terra killed Grux three times. Unstoppable Force cleanses debuffs and adds both armors and tenacity, so when Terra slams the helmet down, Grux swaps onto a softer target until that buff ends.
83030cb5-610d-41c6-9fe4-fbbcaaffbe8e: Aurora brought serious jungle damage: the second-most objective damage in the game, hero damage per minute above the recorded Aurora norm, and Countess dead to Aurora twice.

Six deaths is nearly double the recorded Aurora norm, and Countess got three, eating off Aurora like an open buffet. When Countess has not shown on the map, Aurora holds Glacial Charge as the exit, not the opener.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Mr_Meat31 led the whole game in objective damage and killed Sparrow three times on Murdock. Top objective damage plus repeated kills on the enemy carry is the carry job done. Keep that shit.

Sparrow also killed Murdock three times. Heightened Senses turns Sparrow invisible and then adds attack speed, so when Sparrow vanishes, Murdock places a Static Trap underfoot and backs toward Steel before trading again.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy Guggenheim ran a clean, rich mid game: the fewest deaths on the team, farm and hero damage per minute well above the recorded Gadget norm, and the second-most gold in the game.

Lt. Belica killed Gadget once and died to Gadget twice. Seismic Assault stuns in a line, so Gadget waits for that stun to be spent, then roots Lt. Belica with Security Gate and drops Tesla Dome on the spot.

synergy: Our engage/CC: Grux Crush (knockup 0.5s), Gadget Security Gate (root 1s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

fedBy: Tithe of Death (minor): Takedowns restore 15% Max Mana and permanently grant 2 Ability Haste, up to 30 Ability Haste.
lines: Lead story: Damage well above normal. 1,510 hero damage a minute, more than 98% of Countess jungle players this patch (33% of the team's). The damage came from Megacosm, Combustion, Wraith Leggings.
Lesson: takedowns were the fuel. Each one Countess touched shortened Feast, so feeding early made it come back faster (about 50.6s late); fight right after Feast is spent.
Feast at rank 3: 85s base, about 50.6s by the end (40% shorter) from 68 ability haste: Megacosm 10, Noxia 20, Soulbearer 8, Tithe of Death (minor) 30.
Tithe of Death (minor): 2 per takedown, 16 takedowns, capped at 30 from the 15th takedown, around 28 min (estimate).
16 takedowns (9 kills, 7 assists) fed: Tithe of Death (minor).
Countess dealt 61,926 hero damage, 33% of their team's, with +490 magical power from items.

Penetration: Combustion 9, Wraith Leggings 11; against Aurora (level 18: about 62 magical armor, 42 after penetration; took 32,706 magical damage from heroes, 65% of all hero damage they took) and Murdock (level 18: about 48 magical armor, 28 after penetration; took 12,808 magical damage from heroes, 49% of all hero damage they took) that is about 14% and 16% more damage (estimate: percent penetration taken before flat).
Megacosm (item): On dealing Ability Damage: Deal 2.5% of Target's Max Health as Damage over 3s. Additional applications refresh the duration.
Megacosm (item): On dealing Ability Damage to Heroes: Deal 6% of Target's Bonus Health as Damage over 3s.
Combustion (item): On dealing Ability Damage: Deal 50 (+18%) Damage to the Target and nearby Enemies.
Wraith Leggings (item): Against Heroes below 40% Health: Abilities deal 12% bonus Magical Damage.
Noxia (item): Deal 6% of Target's Maximum Health as bonus Damage.
Vesh (Eternal): Ability damage dealt to Enemy Heroes deals 7% (+0.4% a minute, about 23.4% by the end) of that damage as a DoT over 3s.
Mind Rot (Eternal minor): The major also deals 2% of the target's current health as bonus damage.
Sanguine Slash (augment): Blade Siphon deals 20% more damage and heals 50% more against Isolated Targets.
Sustain: Soulbearer: Gain a 100 (+35) (+6%) Shield for 8s. Gain 20% Magical Lifesteal and 10% Movement Speed for 8s.; 33,192 healing recorded.
Toughness: +250 health; took 89,281 damage, mitigated 58,996, died 10 times.

Stack (Every ability hit set off): 6 effects on one trigger: Megacosm, Combustion, Wraith Leggings, Noxia, Vesh, Mind Rot. Countess has 4 damaging abilities (Blade Siphon, Shadow Slip, Eventide hit an area, so one cast sets them off on several heroes), and 68 ability haste brought them back 40% sooner: more casts, more triggers.
Stack (Damage that scales with our health): 3 effects on one trigger: Megacosm, Noxia, Mind Rot. The more health a target stacks, the more these deal, so health items on our side fed them.
Stack (Healing off the damage): 2 effects on one trigger: Soulbearer, Sanguine Slash.
The Eternal was part of it: Vesh (Tithe of Death + Mind Rot) sits on the same triggers as the items (every ability hit set off; damage that scales with our health), so the same hits paid out twice.

Countered? 2 of the 5 players Countess killed built magical armor (Grux, Steel). Anti-heal on Steel, Aurora, Murdock, Gadget. Health items on Aurora, Grux, Steel raised the %-health damage they took. We killed Countess 10 times.
Copy it? Vesh: 44.4% in 612 Countess jungle games, below the hero's 45.6%. It wins less than usual elsewhere: it beat us, not the field.

grux.loadout: Thraex (Savage Strikes + Ferocity), augment Lust For Blood, crest Iceskorn Talons
lines: Lead story: Damage well above normal. 1,581 hero damage a minute, more than 98% of Grux offlane players this patch (29% of the team's). The damage came from Sky Splitter, Mutilator, Augmentation.
Warlord's Challenge at rank 3: 90s base, about 54.5s by the end (39% shorter) from 65 ability haste: Basilisk 20, Mutilator 15, Augmentation 20, Void Helm 10.
Their build heals off damage: anti-heal (the Tainted items) cuts it.
Grux dealt 64,818 hero damage, 29% of their team's, with +167 physical power from items.
Sky Splitter (item): On Successful Basic Attacks: Deal 5% of Target's Current Health as Damage On-Hit. Reduced to 3.5% for Ranged Heroes. Minimum of 12 Damage.
Mutilator (item): On Successsful Basic Attacks: Deal 1% of their Max Health as Damage.
Augmentation (item): On Ability Cast: Empower your next Basic Attack within 4s. Deal (+90% Base Physical Power) Damage On-Hit.

Thraex (Eternal): Mark the last Enemy Hero damaged by your Basic Attack for 3s, increasing your damage against them by 3% (+0.4% per level) and reducing the damage they deal to you by 1.5% (+0.35% per level).
Lust For Blood (augment): Heal for 5-11.3% of damage dealt to Enemies afflicted with Max Bloodlust stacks. Increases with Hero Level.

Sustain: 7% lifesteal; 16% omnivamp; Void Helm: Heal 20% more from all sources.; Savage Strikes: Deal 1.5 (+0.4 per level) Physical Damage On-Hit. Attacking an Enemy Hero increases this by 100% for 3s, stacking up to 3 times. Heal for the damage dealt.; 24,379 healing recorded.
Toughness: +1025 health, +45 magical armor; took 83,420 damage, mitigated 71,180, died 6 times.
Stack (Healing off the damage): 6 effects on one trigger: Sky Splitter, Mutilator, Void Helm, Iceskorn Talons, Savage Strikes, Lust For Blood.
Stack (Every basic attack set off): 5 effects on one trigger: Sky Splitter, Mutilator, Augmentation, Thraex, Savage Strikes.
Stack (Damage that scales with our health): 2 effects on one trigger: Sky Splitter, Mutilator. The more health a target stacks, the more these deal, so health items on our side fed them.
The Eternal was part of it: Thraex (Savage Strikes + Ferocity) sits on the same triggers as the items (healing off the damage; every basic attack set off), so the same hits paid out twice.
Countered? 1 of the 4 players Grux killed built physical armor (Terra). Anti-heal on Terra, Mourn. Health items on Terra raised the %-health damage they took. We killed Grux 6 times.
Copy it? Thraex (Savage Strikes + Ferocity): 50.2% in 2,279 Grux offlane games, above the hero's 48.5%. Proven this patch: worth copying.
